subject: Policy flex request — tiered onramp & credit boundary for BlueHarbor pilot
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@blueharbor.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@blueharbor.ai
Date: 2026-10-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Piloting Redwood — ask on starter credits and packaging flex

Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the Dedicated offering and VPC controls fit our compliance needs. We’re excited to move to a 6-week pilot that will exercise both streaming and embeddings workloads. Before we kick off the procurement cycle, two items are blocking our procurement/legal team:

1) Starter credits / onramp: we need a firm credit floor for the pilot (expected consumption ~2.5M tokens) and a clear way to convert to committed spend if the pilot goes well.
2) Packaging flexibility: BlueHarbor runs sensitive inference in EU and US — we’d like the option to start on a smaller Reserved pool (single region) and scale to Dedicated cross-region if performance validates.

Can you share what levers you have for pilot credits and whether Redwood can provide an explicit limited-time discount for conversion to a 12-month commitment? Legal also asked for an estimated unit price post-conversion to validate their budget model.

I attached a short intro deck and our preliminary SOW expectations. If possible, let’s land numbers this week so procurement can prepare an internal PO.

—Tom
BlueHarbor (Head of AI Partnerships)

Attachments: BlueHarbor_Intro_Deck.pdf (6 pages)

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-13T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Piloting Redwood — ask on starter credits and packaging flex

Markus / Marissa — forwarding Tom's note. Short summary and ask below.

Why this matters:
- Strategic mid-market prospect in healthcare tech (potential multi-region Dedicated deal).
- Pilot expected to convert quickly if latency/throughput checks out — CTAs from their PM and procurement this month.

What they asked for:
- Pilot starter credit to cover ~2.5M tokens (they want an explicit floor so procurement can issue PO).
- A one-time conversion discount if they convert to a 12-month reserved commit within 60 days of pilot completion.
- Start in single-region Dedicated (us-west) with an allowed scale-path to cross-region Dedicated within contract amendment.

My recommendation (commercially balanced):
- Offer $12k in starter credits (covers expected pilot compute and buffer).
- Commit to an up-front conversion discount of 18% off list for the first 12 months after conversion, capped to the initial committed volume (i.e., discount applies to first-year committed tokens up to agreed floor).
- Require a signed conversion LOI within 60 days of pilot completion; credit applied as prepayment on conversion invoice.

Impact to margin (very rough):
- If converted at the floor with 18% off list, blended margin hits ~25% vs our standard target of ~40% for this segment. Spreadsheet attached with assumptions.

Requested action:
1) Markus: need VP-level authorization for the 18% conversion discount and the $12k pilot credit.
2) Marissa: need CFO acknowledgment of margin hit and whether Finance is comfortable with credit as prepayment (reduces revenue risk).
3) Lauren: if approved, I’ll draft a short commercial LOI and a pilot SOW.

Thanks — I can jump on a quick 20-minute call to walk through the calc if helpful.

—Irene
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_impact_calc.xlsx (calculator, conservative assumptions)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-13T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Piloting Redwood — ask on starter credits and packaging flex

Thanks Irene — good concise ask. I support a limited concession to land the pilot given the conversion probability and strategic signal:

- Approve $12k starter credit (operationally delivered as platform credit tied to account).
- Approve an 18% conversion discount for year one, but with the following guardrails:
  * Discount applies only if conversion LOI is signed within 60 days of pilot end.
  * Conversion discount is capped to the initially committed volume (no retroactive discounts beyond floor).
  * Require minimum committed spend on conversion (we should set a floor — recommend $150k ARR equivalent annualized)

Marissa — can you confirm Finance is okay with the credit-as-prepayment approach (i.e., credit posted to account and applied at conversion invoice; if they don't convert within 60 days the credit is forfeited)? If Finance would prefer a different construct (e.g., deferred revenue treatment or escrow), flag it and we’ll adapt.

Also, include a clause in the LOI: Redwood retains right to revert to list pricing for additional regions unless cross-region Dedicated is executed via amendment. That protects our routing/capacity economics.

Irene — go ahead and draft the LOI + a short pilot SOW (2 pages). Lauren, please pre-fill the conversion floor and the recommended $150k floor in the LOI template.

-Markus
VP, Commercial

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-13T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Piloting Redwood — ask on starter credits and packaging flex

I reviewed the attached calc and Markus's guardrails. Finance will accept the credit-as-prepayment approach under these conditions:

1) Credit posted to a locked account code and only redeemable against a conversion invoice tied to a signed LOI (60 day window). If no conversion LOI, the credit is forfeited and recognized as a marketing expense.
2) Require the $150k annualized minimum on conversion for the discount to apply. If they convert at a lower committed volume, discount is reduced on a sliding scale (we'll propose an earnings threshold table).
3) Legal to confirm amendment language for cross-region move (we will not auto-extend discounts across new regions without an amendment).

Irene — Finance sign-off granted on the $12k pilot credit and the 18% Y1 conversion discount with the above conditions. Please include the accounting treatment notes in the LOI and route draft to Legal for a quick review.

Marissa Cole
CFO, Redwood Inference
